properties.name: Low Wray approach road
properties.reason: The National Trust says the road leading to Low Wray campsite is narrow in places and larger motorhomes should take care. A useful warning because it can look like an ordinary local access road on a route planner.

properties.name: White Cliffs of Dover upper parking access
properties.reason: National Trust specifically tells motorhomes and campervans not to use level 4 parking because of a tight bend and abrupt change in level that can ground a vehicle. Use the designated motorhome parking instead.

properties.name: Red Bank Road, Grasmere–Langdale
properties.reason: Single-track with very tight corners. Lake District National Park explicitly says it is unsuitable for lorries or caravans; for a campervan it is a road to avoid by default when an easier route exists.

properties.name: Hardknott Pass
properties.reason: One of the steepest roads in the UK, with extreme gradients, hairpins and narrow sections. The National Park specifically flags it when warning that sat-nav routes may not suit larger vehicles.

properties.name: Wrynose Pass
properties.reason: Very steep, narrow and twisting mountain pass. Lake District National Park groups it with Hardknott and Honister when warning drivers not to rely on the shortest sat-nav route.

properties.name: Honister Pass
properties.reason: Very steep and narrow mountain road. The National Park explicitly flags Honister among the steepest roads in the country; manageable by smaller vans in suitable conditions but not an ordinary easy route.

properties.name: Peak District green-lane / UCR vehicle routes
properties.reason: Unclassified/green-lane routes can appear routable but may be rocky, rutted, narrow or subject to Traffic Regulation Orders. Peak District guidance specifically says not to use roads too narrow for your vehicle and to check the relevant highway authority.

properties.name: Dartmoor minor-road sat-nav routes
properties.reason: Minor cross-moor lanes can look attractive as shortcuts but Dartmoor guidance warns that some roads are too narrow for motorhomes and drivers should not rely on sat-nav alone.

properties.name: Buttertubs Pass
properties.reason: Narrow upland road with exposed sections and limited passing. It is passable for Transporter-sized campers but deserves advance awareness rather than being treated as a normal B-road-style connection.

properties.name: Fleet Moss road, Hawes–Oughtershaw
properties.reason: High, steep, narrow moorland road with awkward bends and limited passing. It can look like a convenient cross-dales route but is substantially more demanding than the main valley roads.

properties.name: Rosedale Chimney Bank
properties.reason: Exceptionally steep road with sharp bends. Although paved and public, it is a classic example of a route that looks innocuous on a conventional road map but is a poor casual campervan route.

properties.name: Porlock Hill / A39
properties.reason: Unusually steep section of an otherwise ordinary-looking A-road, with tight bends and a long gradient. Exactly the sort of road where the A-road classification understates the driving challenge.

properties.name: Winnats Pass
properties.reason: Steep, narrow-sided limestone pass with bends and tourist traffic. It is a normal surfaced road but is much more demanding than its appearance on a route planner suggests.

properties.name: Cat and Fiddle / A537
properties.reason: A-road classification can imply an easy route, but this is a high exposed moorland road with repeated bends and weather exposure. Generally suitable for a campervan but worth flagging as non-routine in poor conditions.

properties.name: Black Mountain Road / A4069
properties.reason: Mountain A-road with tight bends, exposed sections and substantial elevation change. Suitable for a Transporter-sized camper but materially more demanding than a typical A-road.

properties.name: Gospel Pass
properties.reason: Narrow, steep single-track mountain road with limited passing. A legitimate road but one where route-planner appearance substantially understates the difficulty for a campervan.

properties.name: Bwlch y Groes
properties.reason: Steep, narrow mountain crossing with sharp bends. It is paved and scenic but should be approached as a deliberate mountain drive rather than an ordinary shortcut.

properties.name: Applecross / Bealach na Bà
properties.reason: Single-track alpine-style pass with hairpins, steep gradients and limited passing. NC500 guidance consistently treats this as unsuitable for larger motorhomes; even a Transporter-sized camper should regard it as a deliberate challenging drive, not a normal route.

properties.name: B869 Drumbeg coastal road
properties.reason: Long stretches of narrow single-track road with bends, crests and constrained passing. A beautiful route but considerably more demanding than the A894 alternative and frequently highlighted in NC500 campervan guidance.

properties.name: Quiraing road
properties.reason: Narrow single-track scenic road with steep sections, blind crests, passing places and intense visitor traffic. Technically usable by campervans but easily much harder than the map suggests at busy times.
